newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends easy, gilt prices mixed.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends easy, gilt prices mixed.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday easy at 0.05-0.25 percent, little changed from opening levels of 0.10-0.25 percent on good liquidity with banks, dealers said.
Call rates could move up to 3.0 percent next week as there are three holidays during the week, Vinod dixit, dealer at Centurion Bank said.
Banks in most parts of India are closed on Monday, Wednesday and Friday for local holidays.
"Bankers are waiting for the credit policy as well as the cut-off at the forthcoming securities auction," Dixit said.
"The cut-off is expected to be in the region of 13.25-13.35 percent," he said.
The Reserve Bank of India releases its credit and monetary policy for the first half of 1997/98 (April-March) on April 15.
The central bank also holds the first auction of governemnt in the current financial year on April 21.

Temporary parking of funds in government bonds till the announcement of credit policy and till the results of the bond auction are known will attract buying interest on treasury bills and short-term dated securities, Dixit added
The securities market was mixed on Thursday with prices falling at the start of trade but picking up later in the day, dealers said.
Trades on the National Stock Exchange were worth 5.55 billion rupees on Thursday against Wednesday's 3.35 billion.

The 13.62 percent government stock was much in demand with trades of more than 1.0 billion rupees in a price range of 104.00 rupees to 104.40 rupees against its previous traded price of 105.0 rupees, dealers said.
The 13.50 percent 1997 stock fell to 101.95 rupees from 102.15 while the zero coupon bond maturing in 2000 rose to 68.65 rupees from 68.55, dealers said.
The 364-day treasury bill maturing in April 1998 yielded 9.20-9.25 percent against its Wednesday auction yield of 9.45 percent, dealers said.
Bank of Nova Scotia certificates of deposit maturing in May 1997 were traded at 7.0 percent, dealers said.
